findings.text: Routine kvm_gmem_get_pfn resolves a guest frame to a host frame number with optional refcounted page and order hint, validating the slot binding and ensuring contents are current before returning.
Routine kvm_arch_gmem_make_private forwards a private conversion request for a guest range to the x86 backend implementation.
Predicate kvm_find_async_pf_gfn reports whether a guest frame is already recorded in the per vcpu async fault tracking table.
Predicate kvm_can_do_async_pf decides whether async fault handling is currently allowed based on interrupt and exception state plus halt delivery feasibility.
Routine __kvm_faultin_pfn resolves a guest frame through the follow path, producing writability and optional refcounted page outputs.
Routine kvm_handle_page_fault serves as the architected fault entry, separating synchronous faults from host async wake completions and flagging unexpected host flags.
Routine kvm_mmu_page_fault dispatches page faults across reserved MMIO, generic mapping, write protection and emulation outcomes while maintaining fault statistics.

Entry kvm_handle_page_fault validates address and error widths, requests a speculative side channel flush, then either traces and handles a fresh fault or sleeps for a not present host async completion with interrupts briefly masked.

Entry kvm_mmu_page_fault requires a valid root, applies a private access adjustment for software protected guests, handles reserved faults as potential MMIO, then falls through to mapping with emulation as final fallback.
Entries direct_page_fault and nonpaging_page_fault implement direct mapping; the nonpaging variant additionally caps the mapping level to two megabyte pages before delegating.
Paravirtual async enablement holds only when both the enabled indicator and the interrupt delivery indicator are present in the control value.
Async delivery is denied when the feature is disabled, and without the always send option it is also denied for protected guests or when current privilege is zero.
Nested guests receive async faults only after opting into pf vmexit delivery, while non nested guests receive them only when paging is enabled as shown by the paging status bit.
Guest memory file index equals the guest frame offset from the slot base added to the slot file offset.
File backed memory defaults to private unless the init shared flag is present on the file.
Host frame for an indexed page equals the folio base frame plus the index remainder within the folio extent.
Fault resolution initializes writability to false and page output to null and treats missing output storage as a programming error.
Read only slots force the mapping writability result to false and suppress further writability reporting.
A frame number carrying any error mask bit is classified as an error frame.
Guest memory faults require a guest memfd slot, otherwise they request a userspace memory fault exit; writability follows absence of read only marking and mapping level follows the reported order.
Fault handling snapshots the invalidation sequence with an ordering barrier before checking private versus shared consistency, and mismatches request a userspace memory fault exit.
Accesses to the APIC access private slot in nested mode are treated as slotless MMIO emulation, and when acceleration is inactive they emulate directly without creating a cached MMIO mapping.
Async frame lookup hashes the frame number then linearly probes a bounded per vcpu table until match or an all ones empty marker, staying within capacity.
Async handling is refused when the in kernel LAPIC is absent, reinjection is pending, an exception is pending, the guest is halted without deliverability, or interrupts are not allowed.
Reinjection is required when an exception is marked injected or an interrupt is marked injected or a non maskable interrupt is marked injected.
A fault is stale when its shadow root is obsolete, when a rootless special root has a pending obsolete root free request, or when a relevant invalidation overlaps the frame under lock.
Architected fault address and error inputs are limited to low thirty two bits with truncation warnings, while synthetic fault flags occupy only high bits to avoid collision.
Folio acquisition first attempts to lock an already present folio, otherwise looks up the shared policy and allocates a locked folio, warning if immediate huge order appears.
Faults hitting a slot being deleted or moved retry, except prefaults which return an again status to userspace; missing slots delegate to the no slot handler.
Releasing a faulted page asserts that the MMU lock is held except on the unused retry path where the caller already gave up the mapping.
Marking folios dirty must happen under the MMU lock because of writeback races, so lockless fast faults only speculatively record writability for later handling under lock.
The checked invalidation retry test requires the MMU lock held and treats missing range bounds during progress as a bug, while the unsafe test uses volatile reads for lock free pre checks.
Direct fault handling acquires the MMU lock in write mode across page availability, staleness validation and mapping, then finishes page accounting before releasing.
Internal guest memory lookup returns with the folio locked, and the outer getter keeps it locked across zeroing and private conversion before unlocking exactly once.
Per vcpu async state comprises an enable control value, a fixed capacity array of tracked guest frames, and host side flags distinguishing fresh faults from completions.

A page fault descriptor carries slot, guest frame, fault address, resolved host frame, refcounted page, write and prefetch intents, writability result, max mapping level, private flag and invalidation sequence snapshot.
A memory slot carries an identifier, flag bits, base guest frame, and guest memory file linkage with file offset used for index translation.
Virtual machine invalidation state comprises a monotonically advanced sequence, a progress indicator, and a guest frame interval describing the range possibly being invalidated.
A follow frame request bundles slot, guest frame, follow flags, translated host address scratch space, and output locations for writability and refcounted page.

Fault resolution progresses through continue to mapping, retry to reenter, emulate or write protected detours, and negative errors to userspace, with continue used only internally before final mapping.

When host resolution needs input output, non prefetch faults capable of async handling either halt and retry on duplicate frames or set up async handling and retry, otherwise they retry synchronously with blocking and interruptible lookup.

Guest memory acquisition validates file identity and slot binding, locks the folio, rejects poisoned entries, derives the frame, clears stale contents and marks current, optionally converts to private, then unlocks and returns the indexed page or drops on failure.
Page release is a no operation for null, releases as unused on the retry path, otherwise releases as dirty when writable mapping occurred and as clean otherwise.

Top level MMU dispatch tries reserved MMIO first, then generic fault handling with taken counting, then write protection fixup, then records fixed versus emulate versus spurious outcomes before emulating when required.
A slot file pointer that differs from the expected file or a binding table entry that differs from the expected slot indicates use after rebind and must warn and fail rather than map.
Hardware poisoned folios must be unlocked and reference dropped and reported as poison errors, never installed into guest mappings.
Folios not yet marked current must be zeroed before being marked current to avoid exposing stale host contents to the guest.

Invalidations racing fault resolution are checked before lookup, after lookup to avoid lock contention, and finally under lock, because early lock free checks can miss updates and stale mappings must not be installed.

Aliased guest frames, dummy roots, invalid special roots, unexpected host async flags, and oversized address or error inputs signal programming or protocol errors and take fault or retry paths with warnings.
Read only violations and missing slot translations yield distinct error encodings that must be routed to error versus no slot handlers instead of being mapped directly.
Async control uses distinct bits for enabled, interrupt delivery, always send, and pf vmexit delivery to govern enablement and routing.
Slot configuration uses guest memfd, read only and invalid indicators plus a reserved APIC access private slot identifier to select memory fault versus emulation paths.
Fault handling uses distinct result codes for continue, retry, emulate, write protected, fixed, spurious and invalid to drive the state machine.
Frame resolution uses an error mask plus distinct encodings for needs input output, read only fault, no slot and host address errors.
Fault classification uses private access, reserved mask and synthetic mask error bits plus a host reason for page not present completions.
Lookup and mapping use write, nowait and interruptible follow modifiers plus an all access mask, a two megabyte cap, and a paging enabled processor bit.
Scheduling and capacity use an async halt request, an obsolete roots free request, and a per vcpu async tracking capacity.
